_about.what: The intake for one complaint. Every value that came from a document carries the reading id that supports it ("source": "R12"); anything the person typed carries "source": "typed". A value left "" or null is missing and the validator says so. The keys under _about explain each field; the scripts ignore _about. Delete the sample entries you do not fill.
_about.filingDate: The planned filing date, written YYYY-MM-DD. It prints in the caption, the limitations window is measured back from it, and the student's age is computed on it.
_about.runMeta: The model id and effort setting that ran the skill, for the verification report ("claude-…", "max").
_about.student.dob: As the document writes it ("11/03/2017"); the pleading prints it in full and computes the age.
_about.student.district: The local educational agency as the documents name it. It prints as the respondent unless student.respondent is set.
_about.student.respondent: Optional: how the respondent prints when it is not the district line as read — a Board of Education where the state's form names one, a city-wide agency. { "value", "source": "typed" | "R.." }.
_about.student.county: Optional: the county, where the state's form puts it in the caption (North Carolina's COUNTY OF ___). { "value", "source": "typed" | "R.." }. Prints as a third caption line.
_about.student.homeless: true for a student with no fixed address; then student.homelessContact = { "value": "the contact information to use", "source": "typed" | "R.." } is required in place of the address (34 C.F.R. § 300.508(b)(4)).
_about.parent.second: Optional: when two parents file together, { "first": { "value", "source" }, "last": { "value", "source" } }. The caption, the defined term (Parents) and the pro se signature block follow.
_about.parent.phone / parent.email: From a reading where a document carries them, otherwise typed. They print in section II and the pro se signature block.
_about.mediation: "requested" | "declined" | null (not stated). Prints under Requests concerning the hearing only when set.
_about.expedited: true only with a discipline claim (34 C.F.R. § 300.532(c)).
_about.hearing: Optional: interpreter and accommodations as { "value", "source": "typed" }. Typed text is held to the pleading's voice by the draft gate.
_about.representation: "type": "pro-se" with "counsel": null, or "type": "counsel" with the counsel block: name, barNumber, barJurisdiction, firmName, firmAddress, firmPhone, firmEmail; barLabel is optional ("Registration No." where the jurisdiction issues one) and defaults to "Bar No.".
_about.facts: The person's four statements, in their words, under these fixed labels. F1–F4 are sources the draft may cite ([F1]); a date or figure that rests on them alone is named in sources.md.
_about.claims: In the order they print, each { "id" } from references/claims.json. A procedural claim adds "impact": one to three tagged sentences on how the failure impeded the student or the Parent's participation (34 C.F.R. § 300.513(a)(2)). A catalogue claim may be reworded with "heading", "clause" and/or "cfr" (printed as typed, marked in sources.md). A claim outside the catalogue is { "id": "other", "heading", "clause", "cfr", "isProcedural" }.
_about.relief: In the order they print, each { "id" } from references/relief.json, with "detail" — the remedy in the pleading's own words, the person's quantities — and "sources": what the words rest on, the person's own statement of the relief (F4) and any readings. The draft gate holds each detail to the pleading rules and to its sources. Counsel's fees reservation is { "id": "attorneys-fees", "detail": "" } for the standard sentence.
_about.events: The chronology: { "id": "E1", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" (or "YYYY-MM"), "what": one sentence that reads after "On <date>,", "sources": ["R..", "F.."] }. The date must be written in a source the event names. It prints as the Statement of facts, oldest first.
_about.additionalContents: One entry per item the state block lists as required beyond § 300.508(b), numbered by "requirement" (1-based, the state list's order). Either "text" — what prints under the state's section, in the pleading's words, with "sources" — or "met": where the fixed form of the pleading already states it ("the caption", "section II"). "heading" prints before the text; "note" reaches the report only. A blank left on purpose is "text": "____________" with a note saying why.

F1.question: What the district did, or failed to do

F2.question: How the Parent learned of it
